topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: The spot where I used to play, where the tree stood tall and strong, now lies bare. They must have thought the world was better without its shade, its leaves whispering through the seasons. I remember the day I planted it, my hands small and dirty, feeling the rough bark even before it had a trunk. Now, I walk around the empty space, the ground unfamiliar, as if the roots left a shadow that can't be filled. I keep looking up, expecting to see it, but the sky just laughs at the emptiness, stretching out without a witness. I don't know how to fill this gap, this new, silent space where once there was a home.
